# Catalog-first game spawning

Game code uses generated project catalog keys, never transient World mesh
location indices. Include `app/src/CatalogWorld.h` (or the apphost's
include path for `CatalogWorld.h`) and construct a facade with the live
World and the existing `app::AssetManager`:

```cpp
#include "CatalogWorld.h"
#include "project.h" // generated by the project's catalog pipeline

app::AssetManager assets(runtime, engineWorld, device, &renderer);
app::CatalogWorld world(engineWorld, assets);

// Generated project::meshes names are the only identifiers game code needs.
auto stone = world.Add(project::meshes::Stone);
auto second = world.Add(project::meshes::Stone, stoneTransform);

if (!stone)
    std::cerr << world.LastError() << "\n";

// When game-owned instances die:
world.Remove(stone);
world.Remove(second);
```

`CatalogWorld::Add(catalogKey, frame)` loads the asset via the existing
`AssetManager::LoadMesh` path on first use, caching one acquired resource
handle per catalog key; repeated spawns reuse that resource and produce
independent `smvk::MeshEntityHandle` instances through
`AssetManager::SpawnMesh`. The manager resolves the *current* World
location afresh on every spawn. No fabricated index or duplicate loader.
If a key fails to load, or the loaded asset is parked with no World
mapping, `Add` returns an empty entity handle; `LastError()` describes
the failure.

**Lifetime:** `CatalogWorld` is a borrowed facade. The World and
AssetManager must outlive it. The facade releases its acquired mesh
resources on destruction, so game code should destroy its entity
instances before destroying the facade. Resource lifetime remains
explicitly separated from instance lifetime.

## Next API, after Epoch 6c/6d

The eventual ergonomic node API should also use catalog identity:

```cpp
// Intended syntax only; not implemented yet.
auto node = world.AddNode();
world[node].SetMesh(project::meshes::Stone);
world[node].SetLocalTransform(frame);
```

`NodeHandle` generation checks, per-node mesh ownership, and the
incremental World scene must be implemented first. In the current
engine, `ResolveAndFixup_clusters()` recreates world nodes, and a
`NodeId` cannot safely serve as a long-lived gameplay identity.
Adding a proxy that writes bare mesh indices into scene tables now
would silently lose bindings or references on a streaming resolve.

The catalog is the *asset identity authority*. It does not replace
World's ownership of runtime nodes or the generational entity
registries. `project::meshes::Stone` is a generated example identifier;
the exact spelling comes from the project's generated catalog.
